full_judgment:
9. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, the learned Advocate-on-Record on behalf of the defendant petitioner submits that the respondent does not disclose any cause of action and the suit, is not maintainable for which learned Assistant Judge upon application filed by the defendant petitioner rightly allowed the application for rejection of plaint and appellate court also affirmed the said decree, but High court Division upon misconception of law passed the impugned judgment and decree by set- ting-aside the decree of both the learned courts below by the impugned order which is illegal and not sustainable in law. 

 10. She further submits that the plaintiff respondent No.1 very cunningly practising fraud, got the Rule heard ex-parte and upon misleading submission obtained the impugned decree with a direction for the appointment of the plaintiff which is subject matter of original suit and the High Court Division failed to give attention to the legal aspect of the case and passed the impugned decree which caused serious miscarriage of justice. 

 11. It is further submitted that High Court Division beyond jurisdiction virtually adjudicated the case which he cannot do before trial and also illegally allowed the prayer of the plaintiff directing the authority to give fresh Appointment and, as, such the impugned decree should be set-aside. 

 13.The pertinent question is whether the learned Judge of High Court Division can finally adjudicate the case without giving chance to adduce evidence when there is a charge of submitting false school certificate against the plaintiff. The answer is in the negative. The suit cannot be finally adjudicated without taking evidence. The learned Judge of the High Court Division acted beyond his jurisdiction and finally adjudicated the case which he cannot do before trial and he also cannot allow the prayer of the plaintiff directly asking authority to give fresh appointment to the plaintiff from the date of dismissal. 

 14. We find substance in the argument of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner. So, there are sufficient grounds for interference in this case and, as such, the impugned judgment and order dated 11-8-2011 passed by the High Court Division is set-aside.
